title: sch02_timer_polling_test: skip-locked-timer count is 0 (expected >0) and forced-failure rollback does not surface TransactionFailed — 2 blocks
symptom: TC-SCH-02-02 ('scheduler skips locked timers and does not fire CANCELLED timers') asserts skipped_locked > 0 but gets 0. TC-SCH-02-03 ('firing rollback keeps timer PENDING when event append fails') expects error.TransactionFailed from pollDueTimers() after a deliberately-seeded idempotency-key collision, but gets a normal result {fired: 0, skipped_locked: 0} instead — no error surfaced at all.
root_cause_analysis: Not fully traced. TC-SCH-02-03 pre-seeds a conflicting events.idempotency_key row (INSERT INTO events (instance_id, event_type, payload, actor_id, sequence_number, idempotency_key) VALUES ($1::uuid, $2, $3::jsonb, $1::uuid, $4::bigint, $5)) to force pollDueTimers() into a duplicate-key transaction failure, then expects that failure to propagate as SchedulerError.TransactionFailed. Instead the poller returns a normal zero-work result, suggesting either: (a) the poller is silently swallowing the forced DB error rather than surfacing it as TransactionFailed, or (b) the collision setup itself isn't landing before pollDueTimers runs (a commit-visibility/ordering issue), or (c) the poller never attempts to fire the timer at all for an unrelated reason (in which case it wouldn't hit the duplicate key, consistent with the observed zero-work result). TC-SCH-02-02's skipped_locked being 0 instead of >0 suggests either the row-lock isn't being held by whatever concurrent-locker helper the test uses, or the poller's SKIP LOCKED query isn't hitting the intended row. Both questions point at src/scheduler's polling implementation but were not read in this diagnosis pass — needs a BACKEND-DEV-level trace of pollDueTimers()'s locking and error-propagation logic.
impact: 2 of the ~93 real failures in ISS-0184/GH-517's diagnosed set. Blocks the Green-Main Gate the same as every other ISS-0184 cluster. Also a genuine product-correctness concern if the scheduler silently swallows transaction failures rather than retrying/alerting.
acceptance_criteria: TC-SCH-02-02's skip-locked-timer path traced: confirm whether the lock is actually held and whether the poller's query correctly excludes locked rows

TC-SCH-02-03's forced-failure path traced: confirm whether the collision setup commits before polling, and whether pollDueTimers() correctly surfaces the underlying DB error as TransactionFailed rather than swallowing it
Both tests pass against a freshly migrated database
related: ISS-0184 / GH #517 - the holding issue this was split from
notes: Filed per CLAUDE.md 'No Issue Left Local-Only' and ISS-0184's acceptance criteria explicit split allowance. Diagnosis-only pass; root cause not fully pinned, flagged as needing a code-level read beyond this pass's scope.

TC-SCH-02-02.lines: 189-215 (query at 189-206, dead branch at 212-215); PollOutcome enum at 496-500; skipped_locked increment at 148-151
TC-SCH-02-02.description: processNextDueTimer()'s ordinary-timer path claims the due timer with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED LIMIT 1` (lines 189-206). When the only pending/due timer row is held by a concurrent lock (as the test does at sch02_timer_polling_test.zig:577-581 via a manual `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the same row, left open in an uncommitted transaction), SKIP LOCKED causes Postgres to return 0 rows rather than blocking. The code then takes the `if (due_rows.rows.len == 0)` branch at lines 212-215, which does `conn.rollback(); return .none;` — it never returns `.skipped_locked`. Tracing pollDueTimers()'s outer loop (lines 141-154) confirms `summary.skipped_locked` is only incremented (line 149) when processNextDueTimer returns the `.skipped_locked` PollOutcome variant. That variant is only produced by one code path in this file: the escalation-timer branch inside fireEscalationTimerInTx, specifically when the `tasks` row's own `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (line 442-450) returns 0 rows (line 456 `if (task_rows.rows.len == 0) return .skipped_locked;`), and again at line 295-303 when fireEscalationTimerInTx returns that variant. The plain scheduled_transition/TIMER path used by TC-SCH-02-02's WAIT_TIMER node has no equivalent — a lock-collision on the *outer* timers SKIP LOCKED query is indistinguishable from 'no due timer at all' and both produce `.none`. This is a genuine product code gap (skipped_locked is only wired up for the human_task_escalation timer type, not for the general timers-table poll), not a test-setup problem: the test's lock-holding technique (row-level FOR UPDATE, matching the ISS-301 removal-of-advisory-locks comment at sch02_timer_polling_test.zig:571-576) is correct and does cause the SKIP LOCKED exclusion to fire — it just isn't counted.
TC-SCH-02-02.verified_by: Code trace of scheduler.zig plus a real run of `zig build test-integration-sch02-diag` (temporary scoped build step, added and reverted during this diagnosis) against BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test. Observed failure: `tests/integration/sch02_timer_polling_test.zig:586: try std.testing.expect(skipped_summary.skipped_locked > 0);` — actual value 0, matching the traced dead branch exactly.

TC-SCH-02-03.lines: 309-419 (fire_blk error-swallowing block), specifically the `catch break :fire_blk false` at line 338 (appendTimerFiredEventInTx) and the `if (!fire_ok)` handling at 400-417
TC-SCH-02-03.description: processNextDueTimer()'s non-escalation fire path wraps the entire fire sequence in a labeled block `fire_blk` (line 309). appendTimerFiredEventInTx(...) is called at line 338 as `... catch break :fire_blk false;` — any error it returns (including the duplicate idempotency_key unique-constraint violation the test seeds at sch02_timer_polling_test.zig:685-688, which collides with the key appendTimerFiredEventInTx will construct as `timer-fired:<timer_id>` per line 814-820) is discarded and converted into a plain `false`. Control falls through to `if (!fire_ok)` at line 400, which rolls back the transaction (line 408), calls handleTimerFireError (itself fully error-swallowing per its own doc comment at lines 551-554, 'All errors are swallowed'), and then `return .none;` (line 417) — a normal, error-free PollOutcome. pollDueTimers()'s outer loop (line 152) treats `.none` as ordinary end-of-work and returns a zero-work PollSummary{fired:0, skipped_locked:0} with no error at all. SchedulerError.TransactionFailed is declared (line 25-29) and used elsewhere in this file (e.g. line 118, 182, 206) but is never reached from this particular failure path — it is unreachable for this specific trigger. This confirms explanation (a) from the issue's original hypothesis list: the poller silently swallows the forced DB error. Explanations (b) commit-visibility and (c) 'never attempts to fire' were ruled out — the INSERT at test line 685-688 commits synchronously before pollDueTimers() is called (same pooled connection, autocommit, no open transaction wrapping it), and the poller DOES reach and attempt the appendTimerFiredEventInTx call (confirmed by the fact that a zero-work result is returned rather than a fired=1 result — if the poller had never attempted to fire, that would also look like zero-work, but the code trace shows the fire attempt happens unconditionally for any due, unlocked timer, and this timer is due and unlocked).
TC-SCH-02-03.verified_by: Code trace of scheduler.zig plus a real run of `zig build test-integration-sch02-diag` (temporary scoped build step, added and reverted during this diagnosis) against BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_test. Observed failure: `tests/integration/sch02_timer_polling_test.zig:691: expected error.TransactionFailed, found .{ .fired = 0, .skipped_locked = 0 }` — exact match for the traced swallow-and-return-.none path.

confirmed_root_cause.relationship: Independent root causes, same file, same general design pattern (both are cases where a Postgres-level signal — SKIP LOCKED exclusion, or a constraint-violation error — is caught internally by processNextDueTimer() and converted into a silent .none/false rather than being surfaced through PollOutcome/SchedulerError). Not a shared bug; two separate gaps in the same function that a CODE-DESIGNER fix should address together since both concern how processNextDueTimer() reports non-fired outcomes to its caller.

resolution: Fix 1: a second lock-agnostic existence query (same predicate, no FOR UPDATE) runs when the locking query returns 0 rows, distinguishing genuinely-no-due-timers (.none) from due-but-locked (.skipped_locked). Fix 2: only the appendTimerFiredEventInTx call site inside fire_blk now returns SchedulerError.TransactionFailed directly after its existing rollback + handleTimerFireError call, instead of falling through to false/.none; every other fire_blk call site is unchanged, preserving ISS-303's retry/DLQ bookkeeping for all other failure types. Also fixed a latent self-deadlock in TC-SCH-02-02 (exposed only once Fix 1 made the preceding assertion pass) by releasing a row lock explicitly before cancelInstance() runs on a different connection. A genuine concurrent double-claim occurred on this issue (gh_claim.py race, two workspaces independently fixed it on the same branch) -- resolved via git merge (not force-push), keeping this run's more precisely-scoped, design-validated fix over a competing broader change, independently re-verified correct by TEST-RUNNER before proceeding. Verified: TC-SCH-02-02/TC-SCH-02-03 and the TC-SCH-303-03/04 regression suite each passed across 4 total independent runs with zero hangs and zero regressions. Design: src/design/iss0618-scheduler-lock-and-error-signaling.md.
